 Dengue Fever Risk Increases During Rainy Season, Know the Causes and Prevention 
 28 Oktober 2026, 00:57 | Editorial Team 
 MS Hadi 
 Reporter 
 Tim VOI 
 Editor 
 Illustration (Pixabay/FotoshopTofs) 
 Share:
 YOGYAKARTA - A number of regions in Indonesia have started to be hit by rain after a long drought. We are grateful that the land can finally be wet again and the forest fires can be extinguished immediately. However, this season change also brings health challenges that should not be ignored, one of which is the increased risk of dengue fever (DBD).
 This disease transmitted by the bite of the Aedes aegypti mosquito can attack anyone, from children to adults. Therefore, we need to know the causes of the increase in dengue fever cases during the rainy season and what can be done as a preventive measure. The following is a discussion.
Why Does Dengue Fever Risk Increase During Rainy Season? There are several factors that increase the risk of dengue fever during the rainy season. Reported from Continental Hospitals, here are some things you need to know.
Many Water Stains The main reason why dengue fever spreads faster during the rainy season is none other than the many puddles. We can find puddles in various places, ranging from plant pots, old tires, to clogged water drains. Water that is contained in these places can become a location for Aedes aegypti mosquitoes to lay eggs if the conditions are right.
 "We must remember, these mosquitoes do not breed in dirty ponds or waterways. They actually need relatively clean water puddles to lay eggs.
Mosquito Development is Supported by Environmental Conditions Warm temperatures combined with high humidity during the rainy season support the development of mosquitoes from eggs to adults. When breeding sites are available in large numbers, mosquito populations have the potential to increase in a relatively short time.
Mosquito Activity in the Daytime This increased humidity also makes Aedes aegypti mosquitoes more active. This type of mosquito is different from other mosquitoes that generally bite at night. This dengue-carrying mosquito is more active during the day, especially in the morning and afternoon. Therefore, even if you are at home or at work, you are still at risk of being bitten by Aedes mosquitoes.
How to Prevent Dengue Fever at Home During Rainy Season Preventing dengue fever is not enough just by maintaining the cleanliness of the house and yard when the rainy season comes. Reported from the same page, here are some steps that can be taken inside and outside the house to prevent dengue transmission.
Make Sure There Is No Water Stains Check the home environment at least once a week to ensure there are no containers that can potentially hold water. If there are, empty, brush, cover, or remove the items so that they do not become a place for mosquitoes to lay eggs.
 You need to pay attention to the containers used daily, such as pet drinking places, water coolers, or plant pot holders. Clean the container regularly and make sure there are no puddles.
Use Anti Mosquito Lotion You can use lotion or mosquito repellent products to help reduce the risk of bites while at home and outdoors. Choose products with active ingredients that have been approved by the Ministry of Health and use them according to the instructions on the packaging.
Wear Clothes that Cover the Skin When you are outside the house, wear long-sleeved clothes and long pants. You can also use socks and shoes to help reduce the skin that is open to mosquito bites. Although it does not completely eliminate the risk of bites, clothing that covers the skin can be an additional protection.
Use Mosquito Net While Sleeping Mosquito nets can help protect family members from mosquito bites while sleeping, including during naps. The use of mosquito nets while sleeping is especially for babies, small children, and the elderly who need more protection during rest. Make sure the mosquito net is properly attached and does not leave gaps that allow mosquitoes to enter.
 That is a discussion of a number of things you need to know about the increased risk of dengue fever during the rainy season and the prevention measures. By implementing the prevention measures above, you also help reduce the risk of transmission of DBD in the community. If you experience dengue fever symptoms, immediately contact a doctor so that you can get the right treatment immediately.
